newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan unveils experimental docking satellites.
newsitem.headline: Japan unveils experimental docking satellites.

text.p: Japan unveiled two satellites to be jointly launched and used in unmanned docking experiments in orbit, a key part of Japan's proposed contribution to the International Space Station.

The two units, called "Orihime" and "Hikoboshi" -- Japanese for stars in the Chinese Star Festival legend -- will be launched aboard an H-2 rocket in November, the National Space Development Agency (NASDA) said in a statement on Thursday.
The units would be used in the first unmanned docking experiments by remote control from earth stations, NASDA said. NASDA plans six experiments starting in March 1998.
In orbit 550 km (343 miles) above earth, the two units will be separated to a maximum distance of nine kilometres (5.6 miles) and then re-docked.
Japan plans to develop an unmanned space shuttle for carrying devices and provisions to the International Space Station, to be completed in orbit by 2002.
The United States, Russia, the European Space Agency and Canada are also taking part in the project.
The names are derived from a couple in a Chinese myth who were allowed to cross the Milky Way to meet every July 7. In the West, the stars are known as Altair and Vega in the West.
